thread:
alina-finance: Heads-up  invoice from Helvetic IP (Oliver) for a software license/royalty billed to Redwood UK Ltd. Vendor deducted 18% withholding and asked us to gross-up. Invoice also missing Swiss VAT ID. Holding payment until tax docs are clarified.

rory-legal: Royalty vs service matters here. UK12vs Switzerland DTA may have specific articles on royalties. Whos the contracting entity?

alina-finance: Billed to Redwood UK Ltd (London). PO #30214. Invoice lines: License fee 120,000 GBP  WHT 21,600 GBP (18%)  Net 98,400 GBP. Vendor requests gross-up.

oliver-vendor: Hi all  Oliver from Helvetic IP. Our Swiss counsel advised a domestic withholding unless treaty relief applies. We can provide Certificate of Fiscal Residence (CFR) and either reissue as grossed-up or show WHT line. Prefer gross-up to avoid cashflow hit.

ap-payments: Reminder: AP cannot process without vendor tax ID and bank details. Gross-up changes the payment amount and GL coding; procurement/finance signoff required.

procure-bot: PO amendment required for any gross-up. Flagging budget owner for approval.

rory-legal: Please request CFR first. UKSwitzerland DTA typically addresses royalties specifically; some royalties can be taxed in the residence state only. Ill check the treaty article and whether a UK withholding relief certificate is needed.

tax-bot: FYI: W-8/W-9 are for US entities only. For Swiss payees invoicing a UK entity, required docs: CFR, vendor tax reg number, and any UK HMRC forms for reduced WHT at source. Send to finance@redwood.com.

alina-finance: Requested CFR + updated invoice with clear gross/WHT/net lines, vendor Swiss VAT ID, and bank details. Holding payment until docs are received.

oliver-vendor: Sent CFR and invoice v2 (attached to email). Invoice v2 shows: "License fee 120,000 GBP - Withholding 21,600 GBP (18%) - Net due 98,400 GBP". Also added a note: "Vendor requests gross-up to cover withholding".

rory-legal: Received. Initial read of DTA: royalties may be taxed in the state of residence (Switzerland) unless specifically allowed in source state. I'll confirm whether HMRC accepts CFR to zero-rate at source or requires submission of form AP1/AP2 (proc for withholding relief). Escalating to external counsel for certainty.

alina-finance: If vendor insists on gross-up, we need PO + finance approvals. Please estimate incremental cost (grossed-up amount would be ~147,000 GBP to net vendor 120k?). Ill run numbers.

procure-bot: Noted. Budget owner notified. If gross-up accepted, route for approvals will start.

tax-bot: Checklist added: [CFR received, updated invoice, vendor tax id, legal treaty confirmation, HMRC relief steps if applicable, PO amendment if gross-up].

ap-payments: Also confirm whether VAT reverse-charge applies; royalty/licensing to UK may have place-of-supply rules. If reverse-charge, vendor should not charge VAT but buyer may account for it. Vendor needs correct VAT treatment on invoice.

oliver-vendor: Thanks  will add VAT/registration details if applicable and await your guidance. Appreciate quick turnaround.

rory-legal: Will update once counsel returns. For now keep payment on hold. If we can apply treaty relief at source we will; otherwise we withhold or negotiate gross-up with vendor based on contract terms.

alina-finance: Thanks everyone. Holding payment and tracking actions. :white_check_mark:
